name: Required reason APIs
plain: Apple lists APIs that can be used to fingerprint a device and requires the app to state an approved reason.
meaning: Five categories: file timestamp, system boot time, disk space, active keyboards, and UserDefaults. An unapproved reason is a rejection, so fingerprinting uses are fenced in.

android.note: Android has no required reason list; Play bans some identifiers instead.

ios.store_policy: Approved reason codes per API category (for example CA92.1 for UserDefaults app own data)
ios.note: Enforced 1 May 2024. Covers third party SDK use too. Apple has said it targets fingerprint inputs.

limits.headline: Can't use fingerprint prone phone details on iPhone without an approved reason
limits.user_action: Nothing. Apple checks the reasons when the developer submits the app
can: Use file times, boot time, free disk space, active keyboards and saved settings for approved reasons
Include these reasons for third party tools as well
Show the reasons in a file Apple checks
cannot: Use these details to fingerprint your phone, even if you said yes
Use them for any reason not on Apple's list, or the app is rejected
Skip the reasons after 1 May 2024 and still get through review
Apply on Android; Play bans some IDs in other ways
limits.differs: This is Apple only, in force since 1 May 2024. Android has no required reason list.

story.what_it_is: Apple's list of device clues that need a stated reason because they can fingerprint a phone.

marketing.name: Describing use of required reason API
marketing.pitch: Apps must state an approved reason for using certain APIs that could identify a device.

story.for_you: You do not see it. It means apps cannot quietly check things like how long your phone has been on and use that to follow you around.
story.for_makers: The five groups are file timestamps, boot time, disk space, active keyboards and UserDefaults. Makers must pick an allowed reason, or Apple rejects the upload, which kills most casual fingerprinting.

use_cases.example: A game reads free disk space to decide whether to download high resolution art, and states that reason.
An ad SDK that used boot time as part of an ID must stop or state a legitimate reason.
An analytics SDK reads the system uptime to measure app launch speed only.
A fraud tool lists the exact use of each API so Apple can check it against abuse.
A photo app reads file creation dates to sort a gallery.
A developer finds an old library using UserDefaults for tracking and swaps it out.

story.android_note: Android has no direct counterpart. Google limits fingerprinting through policy and API changes.
story.ios_note: Enforced when the app is uploaded to App Store Connect.
